partners.mechanism_chain: MERTK (HGNC:7533) —DISRUPTS→ Efferocytosis and clearance of apoptotic bodies (GO:0001910); Efferocytosis and clearance of apoptotic bodies (GO:0001910) —LEADS_TO→ Thrombosis (HP:0001931); PROS1 (HGNC:9808) —DISRUPTS→ Coagulation cascade (REACT:R-VASC-109647); Coagulation cascade (REACT:R-VASC-109647) —LEADS_TO→ Thrombophilia (HP:0002378); Thrombosis (HP:0001931) —INCREASES→ Coagulation cascade (REACT:R-VASC-109647). Loss of function in MERTK impairs efferocytosis, potentially leading to increased pro-coagulant material in circulation and contributing to a pro-thrombotic state. Concurrently, loss of function in PROS1 directly impairs the anticoagulant function of Protein S, a key regulator of the coagulation cascade, resulting in thrombophilia. Both pathways converge on an overall increased risk of thrombosis.

#### 1. Silverman-Handmaker type dyssegmental dysplasia  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.398)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-9918485)

**Proposed mechanism:** HSPG2 (HGNC:5119) —DISRUPTS→ Extracellular matrix assembly (GO:0031012); Extracellular matrix assembly (GO:0031012) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal extracellular matrix organization (HP:0003671); Abnormal extracellular matrix organization (HP:0003671) —LEADS_TO→ Skeletal abnormalities (HP:0000960); MERTK (HGNC:15057) —DISRUPTS→ Extracellular matrix assembly (GO:0031012); Extracellular matrix assembly (GO:0031012) —LEADS_TO→ Dyssegmental dysplasia (MONDO:0009140). Loss-of-function mutations in HSPG2 (Disease A) and MERTK (Disease B) both disrupt the critical pathway of extracellular matrix assembly, leading to overlapping phenotypic consequences of skeletal abnormalities and dyssegmental dysplasia.

**How to falsify it:** If genetic studies reveal that mutations in MERTK do not impact extracellular matrix assembly or that HSPG2 mutations do not lead to skeletal abnormalities, this hypothesis would be falsified. Additionally, if common pathogenic variants in MERTK or HSPG2 are found at a high frequency in gnomAD, it would challenge their role as rare disease-causing genes.

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared pathway of extracellular matrix assembly as a convergence point for these two distinct genetic disorders could reveal novel therapeutic targets for conditions characterized by skeletal dysplasias and connective tissue defects. Modulating components of this pathway might offer a generalized approach to ameliorating symptoms across a spectrum of related diseases.

Pathogenic variants in UBA1 disrupt the ubiquitin-proteasome system, leading to hematological abnormalities and inflammatory responses in VEXAS syndrome. Similarly, pathogenic variants in MERTK, which is also regulated by ubiquitination via UBA1, disrupt the same ubiquitin-proteasome system, resulting in phenotypes such as macular degeneration in MONDO:0013469. The shared convergence on the ubiquitin-proteasome system (GO:0000422) links these two diseases mechanistically.

**How to falsify it:** If a significant proportion of patients with MONDO:0013469 do not carry variants in MERTK or genes directly upstream/downstream of the ubiquitin-proteasome system, or if VEXAS syndrome patients do not show evidence of UBA1 dysfunction, this hypothesis would be falsified. _(variant: rs72550401 (common variant in UBA1))_
